thread:
incident-bot: Pager: HIGH — multiple container restarts in runtime-prod-gpupool-7 due to GPU OOM during prefill. Autoscale not keeping up. Node IDs: gpu-node-17,gpu-node-19. Alert triggered at 2026-03-15T02:34:16Z :rotating_light:
Ingrid (oncall): saw it. getting paged. attaching logs from the agent.
Paul (sre): thx. is this tied to the new long-context model rollout?
Nate (runtime): yes, we rolled v2-large-context to prod ~00:30Z. Prefill buffer growth + some 100k-token user sessions.
Cecilia (infra): autoscaler reports spike but scaling cooldown prevented new nodes.
Ingrid (oncall): impact: increased 5xx and container restarts, some customer requests failed mid-stream. CS notified?
Eli (cs): getting complaints from a customer on shared-prod with long prompts, they've opened a ticket. Marking as potential customer-impact.
Paul (sre): grab logs:
```
[kernel] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 79, pid=12345, GPU has fallen off the bus
runtime: CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_ADDRESS at prefill.c:412
container: OOMKilled by kernel OOM killer (oom_score_adj=0)
```
Nate (runtime): that matches prefill allocation blowup. Prefill KV cache ramped to full model size *and* some pinned contexts.
Ingrid (oncall): mitigation idea: temporarily disable large-context variant routing, revert traffic to v2-base; we can also enable prefill trimming. Thoughts?
Nate (runtime): steps we can take now: 1) disable v2-large-context in router 2) set PREFILL_TRIM=true on runtime config (hot toggle) 3) patch per-request prefill cap env PREFILL_MAX_TOKENS=2048 4) drain affected nodes for restart.
Paul (sre): do we have a hotpatch command for PREFILL_TRIM? DeployBot: executing flagflip.
DeployBot: Executing: curl -X POST https://controlplane/api/flags/prefill-trim -d '{"enabled":true}'
DeployBot: OK 200. FLAG PREFILL_TRIM enabled.
Nate (runtime): toggled. Also pushing env change to hotpatch group: `kubectl set env deployment/runtime --namespace prod PREFILL_MAX_TOKENS=2048`
Paul (sre): issuing drain on gpu-node-17 to recycle containers: `kubectl drain gpu-node-17 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data`
Cecilia (infra): draining now. will restart node after pods evict.
Ingrid (oncall): routing: temporarily redirect model_alias: v2-large-context -> v2-base by putting a 100% rule in routing policy.
Nate (runtime): applied route change: `PATCH /router/aliases/v2-large-context` -> target `v2-base` ; now at 100% traffic.
incident-bot: Automated metric spike detection: p95 latency decreased after route change from 1200ms -> 340ms.
Eli (cs): informing affected customers: "We're mitigating an issue affecting long-context requests; temporary fallback to standard model is in place. Root cause under investigation."
Paul (sre): logs after toggles show fewer OOMs but one GPU node still exhibiting CUDA resets. attaching recent snippet:
```
[2026-03-15T02:45:01Z] cuda: failed to allocate 7.2G for KV cache, attempting eviction
[2026-03-15T02:45:02Z] nvml: GPU 0: Xid 79, driver reset
container runtime: restart count=3
```
Nate (runtime): that's likely fragmentation + driver hitting a bug under high allocation churn. plan: drain gpu-node-19 as well, rotate drivers if it persists.
Cecilia (infra): draining gpu-node-19 now. also bumping autoscaler pool target to +2 while cooldown is lowered for 10m.
Ingrid (oncall): are we seeing customer errors stabilizing? metrics?
incident-bot: 5xx rate dropped from 4.8% -> 0.6% in last 8 minutes. pod restart rate decreased.
Paul (sre): manual patch landed: added an eviction policy change to prefer prefix-KV eviction earlier (hotfix id hotfix/evict-prefix-0301).
Nate (runtime): note: eviction reduces memory pressure but increases token recompute. acceptable as short-term mitigation.
Eli (cs): customer update posted to the ticket and status page. no SLA breach anticipated but monitoring.
Ingrid (oncall): anything else to do before handing off?
Nate (runtime): leave PREFILL_TRIM on, keep PREFILL_MAX_TOKENS at 2048 for 1 hour, monitor eviction metrics and driver resets. Rollback v2-large-context until we confirm driver stability.
Paul (sre): agreed. I'll keep node rotation scheduled: gpu-node-17/19 restarted and will rejoin once driver health checks pass.
Cecilia (infra): nodes restarted and joined. driver versions pinned to 535.54.03 for this pool pending deeper analysis.
Ingrid (oncall): handing off to daytime oncall @Paul (sre). I'll file a short incident runbook entry.
Paul (sre): taking over. action items: 1) collect `kubectl describe` and `dmesg` from affected nodes, 2) escalate to driver vendor if further Xid 79 repeats, 3) small postmortem run (owner Nate).
incident-bot: Incident status changed to "mitigated" by Paul (sre). Duration: ~42m.
Eli (cs): customer notified of mitigation and fallback; asked to reopen if they see issues.
Nate (runtime): putting a follow-up: add per-tenant prefill caps and add a load-shed policy for extremely large single sessions to avoid single-session blast radius.
Paul (sre): logging final note: PREFILL_TRIM=true, PREFILL_MAX_TOKENS=2048, route alias reverted to v2-base, drained/restarted gpu-node-17/19, autoscaler temporarily bumped. Will start postmortem doc and tag stakeholders. :white_check_mark:
